verdict: Caution: lend selectively to branded, compliant plywood and laminate units with verified GST turnover and tight monthly stock-and-receivable discipline; avoid commoditised veneer and small unbranded plywood units until their working-capital cycle and raw-material sourcing are proven.
title: Kozhikode plywood, veneer & laminates: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Plywood and veneer convert timber and face veneer plus resin and chemicals into boards; laminates are a separate, more brand-led surface product.** Cash comes from selling to dealers, builders and interior contractors, so the cycle is buy timber and chemicals, hold work-in-process through drying and pressing, sell on dealer credit, then collect. **The two raw-material risks are timber/veneer availability and chemical-resin price volatility** [8][10]. **So when a proposal lands, check where the unit buys face veneer and core timber and whether supply is tied to a known source; if sourcing is spot and distant, ask for the last twelve months of purchase invoices and freight cost.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in brand, compliance and value-added grades, not in commodity plywood.** Rating commentary flags high fragmentation and intense price competition in commoditised plywood, with formalisation and brand-led share gains in premium laminates and compliant boards as the opportunity [8]. **Peer results show the plywood segment can grow fast while group margins stay thin:** Greenlam's plywood segment grew 90.7% YoY in the quarter cited, even as EBITDA margin contracted 200 bps to 10.6% [4]. **So when a proposal lands, check whether growth is coming from branded laminate or from low-margin plywood volume; if the mix is mostly commodity plywood, ask for grade-wise realisation and dealer-wise sales.**

## What has changed now
**The data pack gives a split signal.** Kerala GST collections are up 10.3% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1%, a local tailwind [D]. But India-wide IIP for NIC 16 is up 8.6% YoY while down 0.8% Apr-to-date, and bank credit is up 20.6% YoY against that output decline, a gap of 21.4 pp [D]. **That gap means credit is running ahead of output, so when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower's own sales growth is backed by GST returns; if sales growth outruns GST turnover, ask for the reconciliation.** Peer commentary notes chemical and resin cost inflation being passed on, with 18-20% FY27 revenue growth guided [7]. **So lean on first principles and peers for this city, and treat the Merino dealer listing at Puthiyapalam as evidence of a local distribution presence only, not of local manufacturing scale** [3]. ## How to grow safely
**Pursue branded laminate dealers and converters, and plywood units with BIS-compliant grades and documented timber linkage.** Structure as a cash-flow loan against verified GST sales, with stock and receivable statements monthly. **Take every month: GST returns, stock statement, debtor ageing and a chemical-cost note.** Covenant on drawing power tied to verified stock and receivables, and a minimum current ratio. **Avoid unbranded veneer units and traders with no manufacturing footprint; if a borrower cannot show grade-wise sales and a named timber source, decline.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for sales growth without matching GST turnover, rising debtor days, and stock build-up in slow-moving grades.** Also watch chemical-cost pass-through failing in realisation. **If any of these appear, cut drawing power and ask for a fresh stock audit.**
watch: sales growth outruns GST turnover -> ask for reconciliation and cut drawing power
debtor days rise -> ask for dealer-wise collection plan and tighten limits
slow-moving grade build-up -> commission stock audit and reduce limit
cost rise not passed into realisation -> ask for price revision evidence
non-compliant grade found -> pause fresh limits until rectified
